whatIsSection.title: What Is a Local Corporate Sponsor?
paragraphs: A local corporate sponsor in Dubai is a UAE-owned company (100% Emirati owned) holding 51% of shares in a mainland business while the foreign investor holds the remaining 49%. This arrangement exists for certain commercial and industrial activities.

Unlike individual sponsorship, a corporate sponsor is a registered company rather than a person. This provides a more professional relationship, legally binding contracts, and nominee arrangements allowing foreign entrepreneurs to exercise full control over the company.

Through structured nominee shareholder agreements and side agreements, you legally maintain 100% control over operations, finances, and decision-making — accessing Dubai's mainland economy while protecting your interests.

Private legal documents signed alongside the MOA. They confirm you — the foreign investor — are the actual sole beneficial owner. The local sponsor is merely a paper owner with no right to profits, operations, or decisions.
A notarized legal instrument granting you sole dominion over every business decision — bank accounts, hiring, and daily operations. No sponsor approval needed for day-to-day business.
Clauses legally prohibiting the sponsor from interfering with your business. A clear expectation that your sponsor is a silent partner with no involvement in operations, finances, or management.
Your corporate sponsor is paid a fixed annual amount up front with no share of profit or revenue. Total transparency — no hidden fees, clearly defined payments, and full retention of your profits.
Every document is drafted and notarized by lawyers — MOA, side agreements, nominee contracts, and POA. Legally binding corporate contracts give you long-term legal and financial security.

items.q: Is a Local Corporate Sponsor compulsory for all businesses wanting to trade in Dubai?
items.a: No. Local Corporate Sponsorship is required only for specific commercial or industrial activities in the mainland jurisdiction. Free Zone companies and Professional Services still enjoy 100% foreign ownership.

items.q: If I have a Local Corporate Sponsor, can I still retain full control legally?
items.a: Yes. Through structured nominee agreements, POA, and side agreements, you retain 100% operational, financial, and managerial control of the business — legally and securely.

items.q: What is the difference between an individual and a corporate sponsor?
items.a: An individual sponsor is a person. A corporate sponsor is a UAE-owned company (100% Emirati owned) — providing more professional legal structure, binding contracts, and nominee arrangements.

items.q: What is a nominee agreement and what is it about?
items.a: A nominee agreement is a private legal document confirming you (the foreign investor) are the actual sole beneficial owner. The sponsor holds shares on paper with no right to profits, operations, or decisions.

items.q: Can I change or get rid of a sponsor in the future?
items.a: Yes. We offer flexible exit and transfer options — sell your business, bring in a new partner, transfer sponsorship, or upgrade to 100% ownership when laws change.

items.q: Will the sponsor interfere in my business finances or clients?
items.a: No. Our Sponsor Limitation Agreement legally prohibits interference. The sponsor is a silent partner with no involvement in operations, finances, or management.

items.q: Will the sponsor carry out any operations?
items.a: No. All operations, decision-making, and management remain 100% with you (the foreign investor). The sponsor only holds legal shares on paper.

items.q: What happens if my corporate sponsor company's ownership or management changes?
items.a: Our agreements are structured to remain valid regardless of changes in the sponsor company. We handle any required updates and ensure your control is never compromised.

items.q: Does having an established corporate sponsor help with approvals?
items.a: Yes. Our established corporate sponsors help speed up DED licensing, renewals, municipality approvals, civil defence, and industry regulatory approvals.

items.q: How long does it take to get my business license in Dubai?
items.a: Typically 2-4 weeks for mainland setup including the corporate sponsor arrangement. We fast-track the process through our DED relationships and legal team.
